title: Product Technology — Fluid Milk, Cream, Butter, Ghee, Cheese, Ice Cream and Dried Milk
shortDescription: How major dairy products are manufactured and what controls their quality.
genZNote: Every dairy product is just fat, protein and water rearranged. Churn it, curdle it, freeze it, dry it — different outfits, same milk.

sections.heading: Fluid Milk, Cream and Butter
bullets: Fluid milk: toned, double-toned, standardised, full-cream, flavoured, UHT; FSSAI fat/SNF norms: toned 3.0% fat and 8.5% SNF; double toned 1.5%/9.0%; full cream 6.0%/9.0% (verify current text).
Cream: separation then standardisation (25% fat category), pasteurisation, cooling and optional ripening.
Butter: cream pasteurised, cooled/aged, churned (phase inversion from o/w to w/o), buttermilk drained, washed, worked and salted; product ≥ 80% fat, ≤ 16% moisture, salt ≤ 3% (table butter).

Ghee: butter/cream heated to remove moisture and brown solids (desi, creamery butter, direct cream, pre-stratification methods); ≥ 99.5% fat and very low moisture; flavour from lactones and carbonyls.

steps.name: Add starter and rennet
steps.explanation: LAB acidify; chymosin cleaves κ-casein to form curd.

steps.name: Cheddar, salt, press
steps.explanation: Cheddaring knits curd; salt adds flavour and preserves.

steps.name: Ripen
steps.explanation: Proteolysis/lipolysis; Propionibacterium makes eyes in Swiss; moulds in blue cheese.

sections.heading: Ice Cream and Dried Milk
bullets: Ice cream: mix of milk fat, SNF, sugar, stabiliser, emulsifier; pasteurise (e.g. 68.3 °C/30 min or 79.4 °C/25 s), homogenise, age 4–24 h at 4 °C, freeze with air incorporation (overrun = increase in volume ÷ volume of mix × 100) to −5/−6 °C, then harden at about −25 to −30 °C. Frozen dessert uses vegetable fat and is a separate FSSAI category.

Dried milk: concentrate then spray-dry (hot air ~150–250 °C inlet, product temperature much lower) or roller-dry; instantising by agglomeration; moisture ≤ ~4% for whole milk powder; packing in nitrogen-flushed barrier packs to prevent oxidation.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Dairy product technology applies controlled heating, coagulation, churning, freezing and drying to convert milk into diverse products.
keyFacts: Butter ≥ 80% fat; churning inverts the emulsion.
Overrun = air incorporated in ice cream.
Spray drying common for milk powder.

commonTraps: Do not confuse cheese ripening with milk ageing.

sources.name: De Sa: Dairy Science and Technology
